thread:
laura: FYI—since ~08:03 UTC a subset of apac-edge nodes are failing DNS for model-registry.redwood.internal, 5xxs from model fetches. Spike in errors on the GPU fleet.
deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-2026 — DNS egress errors in apac-edge (assigned: mike)
mike: Can you paste the pod-level dig and /etc/resolv.conf from a failing node?
laura: Pod output (from busybox in failing pod):
```
/ # cat /etc/resolv.conf
nameserver 169.254.20.10
options ndots:5
/ # dig @169.254.20.10 model-registry.redwood.internal +short
<no output>
/ # dig @169.254.20.10 model-registry.redwood.internal
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 12345
```
laura: Node-level dig to the managed forwarder (node-local-dns):
```
$ dig @127.0.0.1 model-registry.redwood.internal
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 54321
```
sree: Any recent egress changes in apac? NAT or firewall rules? This reads like truncated/large response -> validation fail or forwarder refusing.
kai: We rolled the new egress NAT pool last night and enabled port randomization on the gateway at 02:00. Could be related.
mike: Can you try +tcp to see if TCP fallback works? Also check if TCP/53 is allowed out.
laura: dig +tcp @169.254.20.10 model-registry.redwood.internal -> returns ANSWER and IP (so TCP works). UDP always returns SERVFAIL.
ops-bot: conntrack: current entries 658k / limit 700k on apac-egress-gw-1 (alert throttled)
sree: If UDP is failing but TCP works, likely EDNS0/UDP size or fragmentation issue. Many forwarders rely on TCP fallback when UDP is truncated; our node-local-dns appears to be getting truncation but not switching to TCP.
kai: I checked NAT gateway logs: many fragmented UDP packets dropped due to 'allow_fragments=false' after the config tweak.
mike: Also spotted an iptables rule accidentally blocking outbound TCP 53 from host netns during the egress rollout: `-A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 53 -j DROP` (rolled by mistake in egress hardening patch) — that would prevent fallback, but you said TCP worked from node-local-dns to remote when forced. Where is that rule applied?
laura: The DROP rule is present in the host OUTPUT chain on a couple of nodes. But the node-local-dns pods forward to 127.0.0.1:53 which then opens a new connection out, so some flows get through; others hit the gateway and are dropped due to fragment policy.
mike: Root cause hypothesis: combination of (1) egress NAT change that disables fragment reassembly/forwarding for large UDP DNS responses and (2) inconsistent iptables rule causing intermittent TCP fallback failure. Together causing SERVFAIL for many queries.
sree: Agreed. Quick mitigation: 1) revert port-randomization/fragment policy on egress gateway, 2) remove the accidental DROP rule on hosts, 3) bump conntrack limit and add healthcheck to forwarder.
kai: I'll roll a rollback of the egress NAT fragment policy to restore UDP reassembly (rolling patch to apac-eip-gw pool). Rolling now.
laura: Removed DROP rule on two affected nodes and restarted node-local-dns on the failing nodes.
laura: After fixes: pod dig shows ANSWER, model fetch error rate down to baseline.
mike: Nice. Add follow-ups: (a) enforce DNS fallback to TCP in node-local-dns config (b) add egress-test that queries large/EDNS0 responses from edge during deploy (c) postmortem to track why iptables change landed in host hardening rollout.
sree: Filed follow-ups: INF-4123 (node-local-dns TCP fallback), INF-4124 (egress DNS fragmentation tests), INF-4125 (postmortem for host-hardening accidental rule).
laura: Thanks team :thumbsup: Let's keep monitoring for 2 hours and close the incident if stable.
deploy-bot: Incident INC-2026 updated: mitigations applied, monitoring period started.
laura: Closing thread for now — will update if anything recurs.
